text.en: 1. These Rules are the Boundaries and Survey Maps (Electronic Transmission) Rules 2005.

3.—(1) The documents specified in the Schedule must be filed, submitted or transmitted in the form of electronic records.
(2) Where it is not possible to file, submit or transmit a document specified in the Schedule in the form of an electronic record, then —
(a)in the case of a document specified in Part 1 of the Schedule — the Chief Surveyor may allow a hard copy or a copy in the form of a CD‑ROM to be filed, submitted or transmitted with or to him or her; and
(b)in the case of a document specified in Part 2 of the Schedule — the Chief Surveyor may transmit the document by electronic mail, post or hand.
(3) The Chief Surveyor must not transmit a document to a subscriber by electronic mail unless that subscriber agrees to accept service by electronic mail and designates an information system for the purpose of receiving such a document served by electronic mail.

4. Before transmitting an electronic record under these Rules, a registered surveyor must ensure that he or she —
(a)has in force a practising certificate issued under section 15 of the Land Surveyors Act 1991 authorising him or her to engage in survey work in Singapore;
(b)is a subscriber; and
(c)has in place an arrangement approved by the Chief Surveyor to pay for the relevant fees specified in the Schedule to the Boundaries and Survey Maps (Singapore Land Authority Fees) Rules 2005.

heading.en: Digital signature to be used for electronic transmissions

text.en:
5.—(1) A subscriber transmitting an electronic record under these Rules must sign the document with his or her digital signature or an electronic signature as the Chief Surveyor may direct.
(2) The digital signature must be capable of being verified by reference to the public key in the subscriber’s certificate.

heading.en: Digital signatures to be used for electronic transmissions by Chief Surveyor

text.en:
6.—(1) An electronic record to be transmitted to the subscriber of a certificate by the Chief Surveyor under these Rules must be signed with a digital signature.
(2) The digital signature must be capable of being verified by reference to the public key listed in the certificate issued to the Chief Surveyor.

heading.en: Consent of land owner to be obtained

text.en:
7.—(1) A subscriber intending to transmit a document in the form of an electronic record under these Rules must, if the Chief Surveyor so requires, obtain the consent of the owner of the land that is the subject of that document.
(2) The Chief Surveyor may, at any time by notice in writing, require a subscriber to produce the consent mentioned in paragraph (1).

heading.en: Date of transmission of electronic records

text.en:
8.—(1) Any document transmitted to the Chief Surveyor in the form of an electronic record under these Rules on any day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday, at any time between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. (both times inclusive), is deemed to have been filed, submitted or transmitted to the Chief Surveyor.
(2) Any document transmitted to the Chief Surveyor in the form of an electronic record under these Rules outside the period specified in paragraph (1) is deemed to have been filed, submitted or transmitted on the next working day.

9. These Rules do not affect the application of any other subsidiary legislation made under the Act to any application, approval, decision, notice, request or other document or information submitted in the form of an electronic record pursuant to these Rules except in so far as they are inconsistent with the provisions of these Rules, in which case these Rules prevail.

THE SCHEDULE
Rule 3
Part 1
Documents Which May Be Transmitted By
Subscriber In The Form Of Electronic Record
1. Application for lot number or SVY21 data.
2. Survey plan, strata survey plan and strata title plan.
3. Any document accompanying an application referred to in paragraph 1 or a plan referred to in paragraph 2.
4. Any correspondence arising out of or in relation to an application referred to in paragraph 1 or a plan referred to in paragraph 2.
Part 2
Documents Which May be Transmitted by
Chief Surveyor in the Form of
Electronic Record
1. Approval or refusal of approval of an application referred to in paragraph 1 of Part 1 or of a plan referred to in paragraph 2 of Part 1.
2. Any advice, receipt, acknowledgment of directions or other correspondence arising out of or in relation to such application or plan.
3. Directives, notices, circulars and other documents issued by the Chief Surveyor in relation to cadastral survey.
